concepts.summary: Series LCR impedance $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$. At resonance ($X_L = X_C$): $Z = R$ (minimum), current is maximum, resonant frequency $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$, and power factor $\cos\phi = 1$. Power dissipated: $P = V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}} \cos\phi$. Ideal transformer: $\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} = \frac{I_p}{I_s}$.
concepts.common_traps: Voltages across L and C in a resonant circuit can individually exceed the applied source voltage because $V_L$ and $V_C$ are $180^\circ$ out of phase and cancel out!
concepts.tips_and_tricks: Step-up transformer increases voltage but decreases current ($I_s < I_p$) in accordance with energy conservation ($V_p I_p = V_s I_s$).

concepts.name: Peak, RMS Values & AC Through R, L, C
concepts.summary: AC relations: $I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707 I_0$, $V_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}}$. Inductive reactance $X_L = \omega L = 2\pi f L$ (current lags voltage by $90^\circ$). Capacitive reactance $X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{2\pi f C}$ (current leads voltage by $90^\circ$). For pure L or C, average power consumed over a cycle is strictly ZERO.
concepts.standard_formulas: I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}, \quad X_L = 2\pi f L, \quad X_C = \frac{1}{2\pi f C}, \quad P_{\text{avg, pure L/C}} = 0

concepts.tips_and_tricks: In a DC circuit ($f = 0$): $X_L = 0$ (inductor acts as short circuit / straight wire) and $X_C = \infty$ (capacitor acts as open circuit / blocks DC).

### 2.1 Series LCR Resonance, Power Factor & Transformers (Resonance & Transformers)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **17 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: Series LCR impedance $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$. At resonance ($X_L = X_C$): $Z = R$ (minimum), current is maximum, resonant frequency $\omega_0 = \frac{1}{\sqrt{LC}}$, and power factor $\cos\phi = 1$. Power dissipated: $P = V_{\text{rms}} I_{\text{rms}} \cos\phi$. Ideal transformer: $\frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p} = \frac{I_p}{I_s}$.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
f_0 = \frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{LC}}, \quad Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L-X_C)^2}, \quad \\cos\phi = \frac{R}{Z}, \quad \frac{V_s}{V_p} = \frac{N_s}{N_p}
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Voltages across L and C in a resonant circuit can individually exceed the applied source voltage because $V_L$ and $V_C$ are $180^\circ$ out of phase and cancel out!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: Step-up transformer increases voltage but decreases current ($I_s < I_p$) in accordance with energy conservation ($V_p I_p = V_s I_s$).

#### Linked Representative PYQs:
- **[2026 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"A small town with a demand of $900\text{kW}$ of electric power at $220\text{V}$ is situated $20\text{km}$ away from an electric power genera..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2025 Shift] Q#2 (MCQ)**: *"A series LCR circuit containing an AC source of 100 V has an inductor and a capacitor of reactances $24\Omega$ and $16\Omega$ respectively. ..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2024 Shift] Q#1 (MCQ)**: *"The figure shows variation of $R,X_{L}$ and $X_{C}$ with frequency $f$ in a series $L-C-R$ circuit. Then, for what frequency point is the ci..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**
- **[2024 Shift] Q#3 (MCQ)**: *"Which of the following combinations should be selected for better tuning of an $L-C-R$ circuit used for communication?..."* — **Correct Answer: N/A**

### 2.2 Peak, RMS Values & AC Through R, L, C (AC Fundamentals)
- **Exam Weightage**: Tested in **15 PYQs** (Very High Yield)
- **Conceptual Summary**: AC relations: $I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}} \approx 0.707 I_0$, $V_{\text{rms}} = \frac{V_0}{\sqrt{2}}$. Inductive reactance $X_L = \omega L = 2\pi f L$ (current lags voltage by $90^\circ$). Capacitive reactance $X_C = \frac{1}{\omega C} = \frac{1}{2\pi f C}$ (current leads voltage by $90^\circ$). For pure L or C, average power consumed over a cycle is strictly ZERO.

#### Standard Mathematical Formulation
$$
I_{\text{rms}} = \frac{I_0}{\sqrt{2}}, \quad X_L = 2\pi f L, \quad X_C = \frac{1}{2\pi f C}, \quad P_{\text{avg, pure L/C}} = 0
$$

#### Common Traps & KCET Pitfalls
> ⚠️ **Caution Point**: Household AC supply specification $220\text{ V}$ is the RMS voltage; peak voltage is $V_0 = 220\sqrt{2} \approx 311\text{ V}$!

#### Speed Hacks & Problem-Solving Tips
> 💡 **Speed Trick**: In a DC circuit ($f = 0$): $X_L = 0$ (inductor acts as short circuit / straight wire) and $X_C = \infty$ (capacitor acts as open circuit / blocks DC).

## Critical Exam Traps & Recurring KCET Pitfalls in Alternating Current

### 1. Speed & 80-Second Constraint Management
KCET demands answering 60 questions in 80 minutes (~1.33 minutes per question). The most lethal trap is spending 3+ minutes on long algebraic derivations. Always check for dimensional consistency or option substitution first.

### 2. NCERT & Karnataka PU Board Direct Lines
Over 45% of KCET theory questions are taken directly from NCERT / Karnataka PU Board textbook summary points, margins, and standard exemplar questions. Pay rigorous attention to exceptions (e.g., electron gain enthalpy of Cl vs F, acidic nature of boric acid, non-polar symmetrical geometries).

### 3. Unit Conversions & Prefix Overlooks
Units of molar conductivity (S cm^2 mol^-1 vs S m^2 mol^-1), micro/nano multipliers (10^-6, 10^-9), and centimeter-to-meter conversions in optics and gravitation account for the highest frequency of careless mark losses in KCET.

### 4. No Negative Marking Advantage
Since KCET has NO negative marking, never leave any question unattempted. When down to two options, use dimensional elimination or parity checks to maximize expected score.
